assertion_analysis.failure_condition: tests/test_a_worker_cannot_walk_the_crew_home.py:103-118 drives the five measured walks against a synthetic crew home and requires each refusal to name the walk's own root; dropping the resolved root from _refusal_message, or judging the wrong token as the root, reddens it because the guard recomputes the root from the tokenised command rather than echoing the test's input.

The ancestor case reddens when the ancestor branch of _root_is_refused (reckon/hooks/worker_walk_guard.py:139 `root in home.parents`) is removed; negative-control.log shows exactly this case failing at 1 failed/19 passed/EXIT=1.
A cd tracked by the splitter into the crew home followed by `grep -r x .` reddens if _cd_target tracking or the '.' resolution in _walk_roots is dropped.
Each of the twelve recursive-walk forms is asserted refused; removing one program from WALK_PROGRAMS or one letter from GREP_WALK_LETTERS/LS_WALK_LETTERS reddens the matching case.

The sync path is driven through cli._configure_crew_guards with include_git_guard=True and both matcher groups are required present; dropping include_walk_guard=include_git_guard in reckon/cli_entry.py:359 reddens it.

The fragment assertion rebuilds the bound command with installer.interpreter_path(script), the same helper worker_walk_guard_groups composes it with, so a change to worker_walk_guard_groups that keeps interpreter_path would move both sides together; the assertion still pins the matchers, the script name and the group order.
